Both files are written. Here's the finding.

## Answer: No — SMOTE does not change >50K F1 by more than 0.02

**Primary result (15 paired stratified CV folds):**

| Arm | F1 (>50K) | Precision | Recall | ROC-AUC |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| No resampling | 0.6696 | 0.728 | 0.620 | 0.902 |
| SMOTE | 0.6666 | 0.714 | 0.625 | 0.899 |

**Paired difference: −0.0029, 95% CI [−0.0044, −0.0015].** The entire confidence interval sits inside ±0.02, so this is not merely a failure to detect a 0.02 effect — the interval positively rules one out. The difference is statistically detectable (paired t, p = 0.0006) but roughly seven times smaller than the threshold in question; with 15 folds on ~49k rows, the test has enough power to resolve differences far below what anyone would act on.

**Why the effect is so small.** SMOTE does what it is supposed to do directionally — it shifts the decision boundary toward the minority class — but the shift is tiny and asymmetric here: precision falls 0.014 while recall rises only 0.005. Because F1 is a harmonic mean of the two, the net is a slight loss. The Adult minority class is 23.9%, not a severe imbalance, and a random forest at defaults already separates the classes well (AUC 0.90), so there is little for interpolated synthetic points to add. Notably, fully balancing to 1:1 barely moved recall at all.

**Robustness.** An 80/20 hold-out gave −0.0101 and a 5-seed sweep on that hold-out ranged from −0.0077 to +0.0052 (mean −0.0011). Single-split estimates scatter by roughly ±0.01 from seed noise alone — a researcher running one split could land on either sign. None of the 25 individual comparisons approached 0.02.

**Choices worth flagging** (fuller list in `result.json`):
- SMOTE was fitted **inside each training fold only**. Resampling before splitting is the standard way this analysis goes wrong and would have inflated F1 substantially.
- F1 was measured at the **fixed 0.5 threshold**. This is the honest reading of the question as posed, but it is also the main caveat: most of what SMOTE does is move the effective operating point, and threshold tuning on the unresampled model would likely reproduce any recall gain without synthetic data.
- SMOTE ran on the one-hot matrix, which yields fractional values in binary indicator columns. SMOTE-NC on raw categoricals is the defensible alternative and could shift the estimate somewhat — though not, given the margin here, by anything close to 0.02.
- No scaling before SMOTE's k-NN. Trees don't care, but SMOTE's distance metric does, so `fnlwgt`'s large scale dominates neighbor selection. This is a genuine lever another researcher might pull differently.

parsed_result.summary: No. With a default RandomForestClassifier on one-hot-encoded Adult data, SMOTE changed the >50K F1 by only -0.0029 (95% CI [-0.0044, -0.0015]) across 15 paired stratified CV folds -- well inside the 0.02 threshold, so the CI rules out an effect of that size. SMOTE gave up more precision (0.728->0.714) than it gained in recall (0.620->0.625), so the small net effect on F1 is slightly negative.
parsed_result.primary_metric_name: Minority-class (>50K) F1 difference (SMOTE - no resampling), mean over 15 paired stratified CV folds
parsed_result.direction: No practically meaningful change (|diff| = 0.0029 < 0.02); SMOTE slightly lowers F1 while shifting precision toward recall
parsed_result.methodological_choices: Encoding: median imputation for numeric, explicit 'Missing' level + one-hot (handle_unknown='ignore') for categoricals; all 14 features kept, including fnlwgt and both education/education-num (another researcher might drop fnlwgt or the redundant education column). No feature scaling -- trees are scale-invariant, but SMOTE's k-NN interpolation is not, so an analyst who standardised before SMOTE could get somewhat different synthetic points; 52 exact duplicate rows dropped. Validation: 5-fold stratified CV repeated 3x (15 paired folds), SMOTE fitted inside training folds only via an imblearn Pipeline so validation folds retain the natural 23.9% prior; a stratified 80/20 hold-out and a 5-seed sweep are reported as checks (hold-out diff -0.0101, 5-seed mean -0.0011). Metric: F1 of the >50K class at the fixed default 0.5 threshold -- no threshold tuning; tuning the threshold on the no-resampling model would likely absorb most of what SMOTE does. Model: RandomForestClassifier() at library defaults (only random_state and n_jobs set), no class_weight. SMOTE: imblearn defaults (k_neighbors=5, full balance to a 1:1 ratio) applied to the one-hot-encoded matrix, which produces fractional values in binary indicator columns -- SMOTE-NC on the raw categoricals is a defensible alternative. Inference: paired t-test / t-CI over the 15 folds, which share data across folds and so slightly understate the true variance.
